name: TriageAI Patient Triage
subSegment: hospital EDs, urgent-care networks, community health systems, telehealth intake
description: A patient-intake and clinical-triage agent: a patient (or a nurse on your behalf) describes symptoms in a structured form, and a Bedrock (Claude) call classifies urgency (low / medium / high / critical), recommends a department (ER / Primary Care / Mental Health / Specialist Referral), surfaces red-flag warnings and clarifying follow-up questions, and routes the case into a clinical staff queue ordered by urgency. A deterministic safe-default fallback applies whenever the model is unavailable, so the queue never stalls and every routing decision stays explainable and reviewable by staff. The same pattern fits any structured-intake-then-route workflow where a human must make the final clinical call.
buildLevelLabel: Custom IaC (FastAPI + React SPA + Bedrock Converse, deterministic fallback)
outcomes: ~2,200–2,900 triage-nurse hours/year freed at 600 intakes/day by pre-classifying urgency and drafting department routing for nurse confirmation — basis: median ED triage ~1.9 min/case (J Emerg Nurs 2025, n=382,027) × an assumed 30–40% time reduction (illustrative; validate with your own numbers)

Time-to-first-routing compressed from a queued manual triage step to seconds — an urgency + department recommendation returns on form submission, against a US ED median wait of 17–31 min (national throughput study, 2006–2016)
Consistent, explainable triage: every case carries a plain-language reasoning string, red-flag list, and follow-up questions a clinician can review — not an opaque score

More than half of US ED visits are non-urgent (NHAMCS-based studies); surfacing those for safe routing to Primary Care / Mental Health / Specialist Referral keeps critical cases at the top of the staff queue — actual diversion rate is clinically validated per deployment and treated as upside, not a committed saving

roi.savings: ~$170K–$225K/yr — illustrative nurse-time floor at 600 intakes/day: ~2,200–2,900 triage-nurse hours freed (median ED triage ~1.9 min/case × 30–40% reduction) at a fully-loaded RN cost of $76.80/hr. Research-backed illustrative, not a guarantee; validate with your own numbers. Throughput / ED-diversion gains are additional upside but more variable.
roi.cost: ~$1,500–$2,000/yr — Bedrock Claude 3.5 Haiku, one Converse call per intake (~1.5K input / ~1K output tokens ≈ $0.005/intake) at ~219K intakes/yr ≈ $1.2K, plus light FastAPI+React hosting (~$300–600) and CloudWatch (~$100–300). No OpenSearch/vector-DB floor (in-memory store).
roi.assumes: Inputs: 600 intakes/day × 365; ED triage median ~1.9 min/case (J Emerg Nurs 2025, PMID 40387689); 30–40% time reduction from AI pre-classification; fully-loaded RN compensation $76.80/hr (BLS, Dec 2024); >50% non-urgent ED share (NHAMCS-based); cost from AWS Bedrock pricing. Research-backed illustrative; validate with your own numbers — do not commit to playbook numbers.

idealCustomer.size: Hospital EDs, urgent-care networks, community health systems, and telehealth providers running a structured patient-intake step ahead of clinical assessment
idealCustomer.volume: Hundreds+ of patient intakes per day where a nurse or front-desk staffer triages urgency and routes to a department by hand
idealCustomer.team: A clinical triage / intake team (nurses + front-desk) supported by a small platform or digital-health engineering group
triggers: Triage nurses are a bottleneck and intake backlogs delay how fast urgent patients are surfaced
Routing to the wrong department (or over-routing to the ER) is driving avoidable cost and patient wait times
Clinical leadership wants consistent, documented triage reasoning — not nurse-by-nurse variability or a black-box score
You are building or modernizing a digital intake / telehealth front door and wants an urgency-classification step in it
Intake data exists in a form/portal but isn't yet feeding any decision-support
disqualifiers: You expect autonomous clinical decisions (this is staff decision-support — a human clinician always makes the final call)
No structured intake step to feed the agent (kit assumes a symptom form with age, symptoms, duration, pain level)
Hard requirement for a persistent EHR-integrated case store on day one (reference is in-memory, by design; persistence is a customization)
Strict on-premises-only requirement with no Bedrock access in any region

customerCustomizes: Triage prompt and JSON output contract in `backend/src/triageai/triage/prompt.py` — the clinical instructions, urgency definitions, and what the model must return
Urgency and department taxonomy in `backend/src/triageai/domain/enums.py` (ER / Primary Care / Mental Health / Specialist Referral) to match your service lines
Intake form schema in `backend/src/triageai/domain/models.py` (`TriageRequest`) and the allowed symptom-duration set, plus the matching React form in `frontend/src/pages/IntakeForm.tsx`
Safe-default fallback routing in `backend/src/triageai/triage/fallback.py` — where cases land when the model is unavailable
Model id, region, timeout, retry, and rate-limit settings in `backend/src/triageai/config.py` / `backend/.env.example` (default `anthropic.claude-3-5-haiku-20241022-v1:0`)
PHI-redaction allowlist in `backend/src/triageai/logging/config.py` and staff-queue branding/layout in `frontend/src/pages/StaffQueue.tsx`
preBuilt: FastAPI backend with `POST /api/triage`, staff routes (`/api/staff/login`, `/cases`, `/cases/{id}`), and `/healthz`
`BedrockTriageEngine` calling the Bedrock Converse API with a single PHI-aware user turn, schema-validated JSON output, one retry on invalid schema, and a budget timeout
Deterministic safe-default fallback (`build_fallback_result`) so the pipeline never hard-fails — failed cases route to Primary Care at medium urgency and are tagged `ai_fallback`
Staff access: passcode → signed, expiring session token (itsdangerous), constant-time compare, Bearer-token gate, plus slowapi rate limiting and a 5-header security middleware stack
PHI handling baked in: name/email excluded from the prompt by construction, allowlist-based PHI-redacting JSON logger, TLS in transit, in-memory store scrubbed on shutdown
React + Vite + TypeScript SPA: intake form with patient/nurse toggle, result view, staff login, urgency-sorted staff queue, case detail with reasoning and red flags, urgency badges
Test suite (65 backend pytest + Hypothesis, 26 frontend vitest + fast-check, 12 property-based invariants) and the full design documentation in `aidlc-docs/`
sharedResponsibility: This kit is an accelerator and a working reference implementation, not a managed service and not a medical device. You own the deployed application, the triage prompt and taxonomy, the intake data, and the AWS infrastructure in your account. Every triage output is decision-support for a human clinician — you own the clinical decision and are responsible for clinical validation, regulatory posture, and PHI handling in production. The reference is a local, in-memory prototype; you and your engineering team add persistence, authentication hardening, and any EHR integration. Scripts and prompts are provided as-is.
